quest.title: The Hymn of Tir Yazad
quest.description: Access the Harvisptokhm through the path of the depths, and complete the final Rite of Ab-Zohr.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Pass through the path in the depths
Reach the top of the Harvisptokhm

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we at the top of the large tree stump?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We went through all that effort passing through that cavern, only to get blocked again?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I have obtained the Twin-Horned Chaplet, so why is the Harvisptokhm rejecting me? This shouldn't be happening... *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, is there something wrong, Sorush? You don't look so good.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: *sob* It's the Twin-Horned Chaplet... Something is... coming in!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Sorush!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, Sorush, wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Agh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, you're finally awake! You really scared Paimon, fainting like you did up there.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I... I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the tree opened up after that, and we followed the path in. This is... the giant lotus, Gaokerena, that Zurvan was talking about, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened to you earlier? Did something go wrong with the Chaplet?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I saw memories that the earth returned to the Harvisptokhm. Countless Pari, Dahrian machines, and human warriors sacrificed themselves in battle against the demons.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: A masked swordsman, a one-armed sage, and our ancient forerunners defeated the monsters that rose from the depths.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Their consciousnesses then joined the Harvisptokhm together with the Khvarena, turning into rain that descended from the heavens.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Dahrian machines... Wait, did things really go the way Nasejuna said they did?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like we'll have to ask Zurvan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. But what should we do now? Paimon remembers Zurvan saying that we needed to clean out the impurities, or something like that...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: We must enter the Defiled Chambers within our god's consciousness to rescue the Spenta Hearts trapped inside the impurities. Only then will the consciousness reawaken.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: In the memories I saw, that place was a boundless void.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If that's the case, how are we supposed to get in?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Come with me. We only need to follow the paths left by the heroes of old, and we will reach our destination.

talks.objective: Enter the Defiled Chambers to search for the Spenta Hearts
Enter the Defiled Chambers to search for the Spenta Hearts
Enter the Defiled Chambers to search for the Spenta Hearts

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With the Rite of Ab-Zohr complete, you then follow the flow of Amrita and leave the Harvisptokhm together with Sorush, returning to the sea of flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You see Zurvan, who is expecting your arrival.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: To think that you were truly able to complete the Rite of Ab-Zohr. Your deeds are indeed the equal of the ancient heroes. Most surprising.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you don't look surprised at all!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Sign of Apaosha has been extinguished, and the earth has been purified. To think that this could be done even without any sacrifice...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The rain was super heavy! That big hole in the sky is now gone, and the withered tree stump's grown back into a huge tree!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your god will definitely suffer less, now that she's no longer being eaten away by those impurities!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About what happened five hundred years ago...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, that's right! The memories Sorush saw showed that there were people from Khaenri'ah amongst the Skeptics who first fought the monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Now, now, there's no need to be so serious. Since you have seen the memories of the past, what I shall now tell you are not tales, but truth.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: A long, long time ago, when I had first awakened amidst the sea of flowers, the skies were filled with anomalies of the dark hollow and there were monsters roaming everywhere — everywhere but this small land of refuge.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I gathered the might of Khvarena according to the divine bird's last wishes, and departed from the sea of flowers to subdue the monsters, until I met that golden-haired man out in the wilderness.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Half of his body had become that of a monster, but I did not sense an aura of monstrosity in him. When I discovered him, he was holding a ring tightly in his hand.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I brought him back to the sea of flowers, and when he awoke, he claimed to be a Dahri swordsman who had only survived because he had been cursed.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: For a time, I traveled with this masked swordsman, and we resisted the Dev that invaded the sea of flowers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A masked swordsman from Khaenri'ah. Do you think that could be...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Oh? So you do know him. That makes my explanation way easier.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Not long after that, people in scholarly garb led by a one-armed sage came forth from lands east of the desert.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: They claimed to have once fought shoulder-to-shoulder with the heroes of Dahri. They said that those heroes had walked their path despite the ill repute they had garnered...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And that it was to carry the will those heroes had borne, and to completely destroy the disaster from the dark depths that they had followed the heroes' path to this place.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Later, we entered a ruin left by the Dahrians together, and there we found machines that had stood against the monsters — machines that belonged to the war-party that had fought alongside those scholars.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Finally, the one-armed sage used documents left by the Dahrians to find a path through the darkness to the Harvisptokhm.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Thus did we enter the tree and use Amrita to purify the defiled skies and earth. After that, the sea of flowers would constantly birth Pari, and the monsters slowly disappeared from the land.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: #Later, the masked swordsman would leave the sea of flowers alongside a {M#young woman}{F#young man} with golden hair just like yours, and the sage went into the ruins underground and never returned.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The humans who remained would forge bonds with the newborn Pari and call themselves the Order of Skeptics as they settled here.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And now, a golden-haired hero has returned to the sea of flowers, and though it is not the one who came before, I can feel that something has begun to flow again.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: This is also why I chose to ask you for help. With you around, I need not fret about going hither and thither searching for a valiant soul to fight alongside us Pari.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The task of teaching humans is a most trying one indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's just because you Pari are each lazier than the last!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Pale Floater, do not include me in this...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well then, since you have finished the Rite of Ab-Zohr, the impurities will not be able to threaten this place for a time — and I can take that time to rest.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: As for Sorush, I leave her to you. Do guide her well in your journey — this is, after all, also the work of a Yasnapati.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I do not intend to be lectured by you, Pale Floater...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, don't be like that! You gotta listen to your teachers, y'know? Still, Zurvan, you say it like we won't meet again or something.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well, you don't intend to stay here with me, do you? You humans are all like that. You will never stop to settle down.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Haha! Well, I'm afraid I shan't believe you. This isn't my first time hearing such words.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Speaking of which, I wonder how that masked swordsman is now... If you see him, do say hello to him for me.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: You are both travelers, after all. I'm certain your paths will cross.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Alright, alright, go off to where you need to be. Don't miss me too much now.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Yes. It is said that the people of Dahri were cursed to varying degrees during that catastrophe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Spenta Hearts here have all been brought back to the lotus. According to what you said earlier, Sorush, we should be able to awaken the divine consciousness now.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: In that case, let the real Rite of Ab-Zohr begin.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Next, I shall borrow the power of Khvarena to make the Flower of Sanctity bloom once again within Gaokerena.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: But this will mean unleashing the filth gathered within the sacred lotus, which will transform into monsters that bar our path.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: It matters not, for so long as the god's consciousness is awakened, the power of the Amrita will defend us.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: If the Flower of Sanctity grows, it will spread Amrita all over the land, and cleanse all its impurities.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: This, then, is a final battle worthy of a Bloomguard!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Spenta Heart comes forth...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back, Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Welcome back. I've received notice from the Akademiya that you were able to successfully solve the problem posed by that strange celestial sign. Very impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I'll say that you exceeded expectations on this count.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Paimon thought you said we were the best choice for this job.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or do you just say that to literally everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Well, of course not. I believed you could do it.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. We did ask you to contact the Nagarjunites previously. Were they of any help to you, I wonder?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: It seems that things got complicated.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: However, it is all ultimately a part of your adventures, and experience is itself an irreplaceable treasure.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Since you've managed to successfully finish that commission, the Guild should now have permission to investigate those Khaenri'ahn ruins. If any related commissions do come up, you'll also get first priority in our considerations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, we've come all this way, but we still don't know who our commissioner was!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Well... The Adventurers' Guild is obligated to keep the identities of those who submit commissions confidential. As such, I'm afraid I cannot reveal that to you.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: However, the person who gave us that token did claim to have been a light novelist.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A light novelist? Wait a moment. Didn't we hear that there was this Skeptic elder...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hmm, it does look like you do know something about this, but well, that has nothing to do with the Guild. Either way, the remuneration from the Akademiya is here with me. Please, feel free to take it.

choices.text: You could say so, sort of...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh! How did the Rifthounds even get here?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: These beings have crawled out from our god's consciousness. She has been bearing their weight all these centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Let us find a way to ease her suffering!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These guys are getting harder to deal with!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If this keeps up, they'll eat the Spenta Heart!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Spenta Heart seems to be regrowing...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The filth has been eradicated, it would seem.
